rejected.title: Ways of writing history
card: People have recorded the past in more than one way. Two main ways are written accounts and oral histories.
Written accounts

Herodotus, a Greek writer, wrote about the wars between Greece and Persia and the lands and peoples he learned about. Sima Qian, in China, wrote a long history of China from its earliest rulers up to his own time.
Oral histories
These are stories, songs and memories spoken aloud and passed from one generation to the next. Many cultures have used them to keep their past alive, and some still do.
Each way gives a different view of the past. A historian can use both kinds of source, and can ask who made each one and why.
rejected.remember: The past has been kept in writing, as Herodotus and Sima Qian did, and in spoken stories passed down through generations.

a.q: Which of these is an example of an oral history?
opts: A story about the past told aloud and passed on in a family
A history of Greece and Persia written by Herodotus
A long history of China written by Sima Qian
A report on the past copied out and stored in a library
a.why: An oral history is spoken and passed from one generation to the next. The works of Herodotus and Sima Qian were written down, so they are written accounts.
a.clue: Look for the way the story is passed on, not just who tells it.

b.q: Priya is studying a people whose past was kept in two ways: a written account and stories passed down aloud. How should she use these sources?
opts: Use both, and ask who made each one and why
Use only the written one, as writing is always accurate
Use only the oral one, as spoken stories never change
Use neither, as only objects can tell us about the past
b.why: Each kind of source gives a different view of the past, so a historian can use both and ask who made each one and why. It is tempting to trust only writing, but a written account was also made by a person with their own purpose.
b.clue: Every source, spoken or written, was made by someone for a reason.

b.q: A historian wants to study how people in ancient China understood their own past. Which source was written by Sima Qian?
opts: A written history of China from its earliest rulers
A written account of the wars between Greece and Persia
A song passed down by memory in a village
A story told aloud by an elder to children
b.why: Sima Qian wrote a long history of China, so it is a written account. The account of Greece and Persia was written by Herodotus, and the song and the story are oral histories.
b.clue: Sima Qian lived in China and wrote his history down.

a.q: Which of these is an example of an oral history?
opts: A story about the past told aloud and passed down
A history of Greece and Persia written by Herodotus
A long history of China written by Sima Qian

b.q: Priya is studying a people whose past was kept in two ways: a written account and stories passed down aloud. How should she use these sources?
opts: Compare the two, thinking about the purpose of each
Trust the written account more, as it was set down
Set the stories aside, as nobody wrote them down
Accept both as told, as people from that time made them
